Summary: Prescribe a scheduled medicine with dose, route, frequency, start and duration
User story: As a doctor, I want to prescribe a scheduled medicine with dose, route, frequency, start and duration, so that the nurse gets an exact schedule.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given an admitted patient, when I sign a medicine order, then dose events are created for every scheduled time within the duration, and the order appears in the nurse's inbox as New.
- Given the patient has a recorded allergy that matches the drug or its class, when I try to sign, then I see a hard stop with the allergy and must enter an override reason to continue.
- Given an identical active order exists, when I sign, then I see a duplicate warning.

Summary: Mark an order STAT or urgent
User story: As a doctor, I want to mark an order STAT or urgent, so that the nurse is alerted at once.
Acceptance criteria: - When I sign a STAT order, then the assigned nurse and in-charge get a push alert, and the dose is due now with the STAT window (default 15 min) shown as a countdown.

Summary: Order PRN medicines with an indication, minimum interval and 24-hour maximum
User story: As a doctor, I want to order PRN medicines with an indication, minimum interval and 24-hour maximum.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given a PRN dose was given less than the minimum interval ago, when the nurse tries to give again, then the give flow blocks with the time it becomes allowed.
- When the 24-hour maximum is reached, then the PRN line is locked until the window allows another dose.

Summary: Order lab and radiology tests with priority and a clinical note
User story: As a doctor, I want to order lab and radiology tests with priority and a clinical note, so that the nurse knows what to collect or prepare.
Acceptance criteria: - When I sign a lab order, then a specimen task appears with tube type, volume and label, due by priority (STAT now, urgent 1 h, routine next round, configurable).

Summary: Write nursing orders (dressing, turning, catheter care, physiotherapy) with a frequency
User story: As a doctor, I want to write nursing orders (dressing, turning, catheter care, physiotherapy) with a frequency, so that they become timed tasks.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: Set the monitoring order: vitals frequency, alert limits and target ranges for this patient
User story: As a doctor, I want to set the monitoring order: vitals frequency, alert limits and target ranges for this patient.
Acceptance criteria: - When I set SpO₂ target 88–92% for a COPD patient, then the nurse's chart, trend band and escalation rules use that target for this patient only.

Summary: Order infusions with rate or a titration rule
User story: As a doctor, I want to order infusions with rate or a titration rule, so that the nurse can start, adjust and stop them correctly.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: Order diet, nil-by-mouth windows and fluid restrictions
User story: As a doctor, I want to order diet, nil-by-mouth windows and fluid restrictions.
Acceptance criteria: - During an NBM window, oral medicines show a "patient is nil by mouth" warning in the give flow.

Summary: Order devices and oxygen with settings and duration
User story: As a doctor, I want to order devices and oxygen with settings and duration, so that the nurse's device timer and checks follow my order.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: Change, hold or stop an order with a reason
User story: As a doctor, I want to change, hold or stop an order with a reason, so that the nurse sees the change immediately and nothing past is lost.
Acceptance criteria:
- When I change the dose, then a new version is created, future doses use it, past doses stay linked to the old version, and the nurse's inbox shows Changed with old → new.
- When I stop an order, then future doses are cancelled and shown as "stopped by Dr X at hh:mm", and doses already given are unchanged.

Summary: Enter a verbal or telephone order on the doctor's behalf with read-back
User story: As a nurse, I want to enter a verbal or telephone order on the doctor's behalf with read-back, so that urgent care is not delayed.
Acceptance criteria: - When I enter a verbal order, then I must tick "read back to the doctor", it is labelled Verbal, and the doctor gets a countersign task; if not countersigned within the configured hours, the in-charge is alerted.

Summary: New medicine orders in a queue with allergies, interactions, renal/weight dosing and duplicates shown
User story: As a pharmacist, I want new medicine orders in a queue with allergies, interactions, renal/weight dosing and duplicates shown, so that I can verify, query or reject.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given verification is on, when an order is waiting, then the nurse sees it on the MAR as "Waiting for pharmacist" and cannot give it (except STAT/emergency, see B2).
- When I query the doctor, then the doctor gets the query and the order stays not givable until resolved.

Summary: Give a STAT or emergency medicine before verification
User story: As a nurse, I want to give a STAT or emergency medicine before verification, so that urgent treatment is not delayed.
Acceptance criteria: - The dose is recorded with "given before pharmacist check" and the pharmacist gets a retrospective review task.

Summary: One inbox of new, changed and stopped orders for my patients
User story: As a nurse, I want one inbox of new, changed and stopped orders for my patients, so that I don't miss any change.
Acceptance criteria:
- Each item shows patient, order, who, when, and what changed; I acknowledge with one tap; unacknowledged orders older than the configured time alert the in-charge.
- The tab or bed tile shows a count badge; STAT items are red, others amber.

Summary: Acknowledging an order to create my work automatically (doses, samples, tasks, monitoring times)
User story: As a nurse, I want acknowledging an order to create my work automatically (doses, samples, tasks, monitoring times), so that I don't re-enter anything.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: A day MAR showing every dose as scheduled, due, overdue, given, not given or recorded in error
User story: As a nurse, I want a day MAR showing every dose as scheduled, due, overdue, given, not given or recorded in error, so that I see the whole day at a glance.
Acceptance criteria: - Due and overdue doses come first; medicines with nothing due fold behind "Show n".

Summary: Give a medicine by scanning the patient's wristband and then the medicine
User story: As a nurse, I want to give a medicine by scanning the patient's wristband and then the medicine, so that the five rights are checked by the system.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given I scan another patient's wristband, then I see a red STOP naming that patient and Confirm stays disabled.
- Given I scan a medicine that is not due for this patient, then I see STOP with the scanned item and Confirm stays disabled.
- When both scans match, then the system shows checks for patient, drug, dose, route, time (late shows minutes), allergy, last-given interval and weight-based dose where configured.

Summary: High-alert medicines to require a second nurse
User story: As a nurse, I want high-alert medicines to require a second nurse, so that errors are caught before the dose.
Acceptance criteria: - Confirm is disabled until a second nurse is chosen and their PIN is verified by the server.

Summary: A manual override when scanning is impossible, with a reason and what I checked instead
User story: As a nurse, I want a manual override when scanning is impossible, with a reason and what I checked instead.
Acceptance criteria: - Reasons: wristband damaged or missing, medicine has no barcode, scanner not working, emergency; note at least 4 characters. Overrides go to a pharmacy/quality report and untick "every dose scanned" in compliance.

Summary: Record "not given" with a reason
User story: As a nurse, I want to record "not given" with a reason, so that the doctor knows and can act.
Acceptance criteria: - Reasons: patient refused, held by doctor, nil by mouth, patient away, medicine unavailable, vomited, other. The ordering doctor is notified (section 2.4).

Summary: 10 seconds to undo a "Given", and after that a "recorded in error" path that keeps the original
User story: As a nurse, I want 10 seconds to undo a "Given", and after that a "recorded in error" path that keeps the original.
Acceptance criteria: - Undo restores the exact previous state; after 10 s, "recorded in error" asks a reason (not given, wrong patient, wrong time, duplicate), keeps the entry visible struck through with who/when/why, and the dose becomes due or overdue again.

Summary: Give PRN doses with a reason and get a reassessment task
User story: As a nurse, I want to give PRN doses with a reason and get a reassessment task, so that the effect is recorded.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: Start, change the rate of, and stop infusions with scanning
User story: As a nurse, I want to start, change the rate of, and stop infusions with scanning, so that the doctor sees rate history and volume.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Epic: Epic E: Samples, results and critical values

User story: As a nurse, I want to collect a sample by scanning the wristband and the printed label, so that the right specimen goes to the lab.
Acceptance criteria: - Steps Ordered → Collected → Sent → Resulted, each with time and user; Collect can be undone for 10 s.

Epic: Epic E: Samples, results and critical values
Summary: A critical value banner and a read-back form
User story: As a nurse, I want a critical value banner and a read-back form, so that the doctor is told and it is documented.
Acceptance criteria: - When I record the doctor's name, "read back" tick and instruction, then the critical alert closes everywhere at once (bell, bed tile, orders badge, compliance) and the doctor's view shows the read-back.

Epic: Epic F: Vitals, monitoring and escalation
Summary: Vitals due times to follow the doctor's monitoring order
User story: As a nurse, I want vitals due times to follow the doctor's monitoring order, so that I check as often as ordered.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Epic: Epic F: Vitals, monitoring and escalation
Summary: Linked monitors to fill pulse, BP, respiratory rate and SpO₂, with each value labelled by source
User story: As a nurse, I want linked monitors to fill pulse, BP, respiratory rate and SpO₂, with each value labelled by source, so that I only check and save.
Acceptance criteria: - If the monitor stops sending, the device fields empty and say since when; manual entry is offered.

Epic: Epic F: Vitals, monitoring and escalation
Summary: The warning score worked out on save and escalation raised when it crosses the threshold
User story: As a nurse, I want the warning score worked out on save and escalation raised when it crosses the threshold, so that the doctor is called in time.
Acceptance criteria:
- The score tool follows the patient: adult → NEWS2; pregnant → obstetric score; under 16 → paediatric score; newborn → newborn score. Only NEWS2 is calculated in MVP; the others are configurable stubs (TODO for the hospital's chart).
- Escalation states: open → acknowledged (doctor replies) → reviewed (doctor documents review). Nobody closes it by hand.

Epic: Epic F: Vitals, monitoring and escalation
Summary: Message the doctor with an SBAR filled from the record and see sent / seen / acknowledged
User story: As a nurse, I want to message the doctor with an SBAR filled from the record and see sent / seen / acknowledged.
Acceptance criteria: - A doctor's acknowledgement also moves the escalation to acknowledged.

Epic: Epic G: Tasks, assessments and the shift timeline
Summary: One hour-by-hour timeline for my shift with medicines, tasks, assessments, samples, turns and device checks
User story: As a nurse, I want one hour-by-hour timeline for my shift with medicines, tasks, assessments, samples, turns and device checks, so that I plan my time.
Acceptance criteria: - Overdue = red, due this hour = amber, done/later = grey; tapping an item acts on it (medicines open the give flow).

Epic: Epic G: Tasks, assessments and the shift timeline
Summary: Risk assessments (fall, pressure, pain, IV site) with due times from policy
User story: As a nurse, I want risk assessments (fall, pressure, pain, IV site) with due times from policy, so that I reassess on time.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: As a nurse in a stage-based area (emergency, labour, dialysis, day care), I want a stage pathway instead of an hourly gr
User story: As a nurse in a stage-based area (emergency, labour, dialysis, day care), I want a stage pathway instead of an hourly grid. (Configured per department.)
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: A guided round bed by bed with a checklist and the items due at each bed
User story: As a nurse, I want a guided round bed by bed with a checklist and the items due at each bed, so that nothing is missed.
Acceptance criteria:
- "All normal" ticks the checklist in one tap; any item marked "act" creates a follow-up task.
- "Patient not available" marks the bed and reminds me to come back within 30 minutes.
- On finish, a round summary is saved to each patient and to the ward rounding log.

Summary: Do the round on a phone offline
User story: As a nurse, I want to do the round on a phone offline, so that a weak network doesn't stop me; entries sync when the network returns, and conflicts are shown, not overwritten.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4

Summary: Arrange my console (drag, resize, hide, add sections), saved for me only

Summary: Start and stop devices with live timers, required checks while running, and a stop reason
User story: As a nurse, I want to start and stop devices with live timers, required checks while running, and a stop reason, so that use is safe and the time reaches the bill.
Acceptance criteria: - Device time per session and per day is posted to the IPD bill using the device's billing unit (per hour / per day).

Summary: A running intake/output balance since the start of the shift

Summary: Write DAR, SOAP or free-text notes with quick-insert chips and dictation, and sign them
User story: As a nurse, I want to write DAR, SOAP or free-text notes with quick-insert chips and dictation, and sign them, so that documentation is fast.
Acceptance criteria: - Signed notes are locked; 10-second undo returns the text to the editor; after that, corrections are addenda or "recorded in error" (kept, struck through).

Summary: An SBAR handover built from the record for each patient, which the receiving nurse accepts
User story: As a nurse, I want an SBAR handover built from the record for each patient, which the receiving nurse accepts.
Acceptance criteria: See spec section 4
